findings.text: The opening three paragraphs tell a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, the problem it solves, and that this page is a study of another project called firstmate. A newcomer can answer "what is it" and "why does it matter" within the first screen.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The first section after the header is an error message. The header promises a commit traced to request, models, cost and verdict, so the one place meant to show that proof shows a failure instead. This weakens the case for Athena at the point where a newcomer is deciding whether to trust it.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: What to do next is clear and linked from the top: the page lists prerequisites, a clone command, an install command and a first request to try. A newcomer knows how to start.
findings.source: Header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself." and Next steps: "git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link speaks to the project owner, not a first-time visitor, and sits next to the newcomer's next-step link without saying who it is for. A newcomer may click it expecting something meant for them.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Almost all of the page covers firstmate's internals (exit codes, transitions t1–t12, 45 claims). A newcomer who came to learn about Athena may not realise the study itself is the demonstration unless they read the second paragraph carefully.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"; sections Transitions, Counters, Claims and sources

findings.text: The firstmate study is easy to follow for a technical reader. It defines terms before using them, walks through one piece of work step by step, and links each statement to a claim with source lines at a pinned commit. That shows the traceability Athena claims to offer.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say they cannot define the term. This is honest, but a newcomer is left with words like wake, endpoint and heartbeat that the page never explains.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a wake." / "The firstmate source does not define an endpoint."

findings.text: This section describes Athena's internal folder layout and tells a newcomer nothing they can act on.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
